clusters.name: Occluded fingers of the grasping hand
clusters.statement: Single-view and egocentric headset hand estimators cannot recover finger-level 3D pose of a hand that is grasping or manipulating an object. Errors rise sharply with object occlusion and self-occlusion: they are worst at the thumb and fingertips and collapse beyond roughly 80 percent hand coverage. Occluded hands are often dropped entirely, and no per-frame or causal method recovers the hidden joints reliably.
clusters.description: Papers repeatedly report that hand mesh and keypoint failures concentrate in object occlusion and self-occlusion. The thumb and fingertips carry the largest errors because they are hidden most often. Even dense dome, multi-view and marker-based annotation degrades during interaction compared with free-hand motion, and hand-attached markers fail under occlusion. Headset trackers (UmeTrack, consumer VR SDKs) lose track during grasps, and detectors miss heavily occluded hands, leaving gaps that are interpolated or discarded. The causes named are the small visible hand area, ambiguity of hidden joints, and harder 2D-to-3D lifting when the object covers the hand. Attempts include new backbones, probabilistic diffusion hypotheses, IMU or EMG fusion, synthetic data and fine-tuning on occluded frames; each gives small gains.

evidence_items.item: Failure cases concentrated in self-occlusion and object occlusion remain challenging; some failures come from a very small visible hand area, others from ambiguity caused by occlusion.
Accuracy degrades sharply under extreme object occlusion beyond roughly 80 percent of the hand region; 2D-to-3D lifting error is higher on hand-object datasets.
Vision-only UmeTrack deviates substantially for occluded, unseen fingers during grasps.
Hand pose errors are largest for the thumb and fingertips, which are more often occluded; ego hand pose under occlusion and out-of-view hands is an open problem.
Annotation accuracy degrades during hand-object interaction relative to no interaction (P90 MPJPE 12.53 mm vs 7.31 mm).
UmeTrack shows inaccurate relative depth of keypoints and complete loss of track during occlusion.
Hands are missed entirely under heavy occlusion by the object or the other hand.
R-CNN fails to detect heavily occluded hands, and interpolating several consecutive missing frames gives inaccurate poses because there is no direct observation.
Human demonstration data relies on consumer VR hand-tracking SDKs that can fail under heavy occlusion.
Hand-attached marker tracking suffers jitter or failure under occlusion even with 70 cameras; occlusion-robust hand and object tracking is listed as open.
MANO-based hand pose estimation is not robust under occlusion and rapid motion.
Hand joints are missing in some frames due to occlusion.
Hand pose methods typically fail when hands interact with objects in complex scenarios.
Exocentric hands are small and occluded by body and objects.

benchmark_evidence: HO3Dv2 / stage-1 P-MPJPE: 7.89 mm vs 5.01 mm on FreiHAND, showing object occlusion harms lifting (1543)
HandSense occluded frames / MKPE: UmeTrack 19.2 mm, 16.6 mm after fine-tuning, vs about 10 mm on non-occluded frames (190)
EgoExo-Hands 30-camera dome validation / P90 MPJPE: 12.53 mm with hand-object interaction vs 7.31 mm without (1534)
DexGloveHOI / MKPE: best vision plus IMU fusion still 10.36 mm, fingertips 13.25 mm (1499)
HO-3D v2 / PA-MPJPE: baselines 7.5-7.7 mm vs 5.5-6.0 mm on FreiHAND; large synthetic data cuts it only 2-3 percent (1130)
Ego-Exo4D ego hand / MPJPE: best baseline 30.57 mm (1190); challenge winner 24.80 mm (1526)
AssemblyHands / MPJPE: best 12.21 mm overall but 16.27 mm on the occlusion-heavy inspect action (302)
DexYCB / MPJPE: best 17.80 mm; AssemblyHands 18.78 mm (1536)
HOI4D / hand MPJPE: best method 41.9 mm (1126)
POV-Surgery / MPJPE before fine-tuning: 77.46-115.67 mm for METRO, HandOccNet and SEMI (1128)
clusters.settings: Monocular RGB single-hand crops (DexYCB, HO3D v2, with FreiHAND for contrast); egocentric headset monochrome or stereo (HOT3D, UmeTrack, AssemblyHands, HandSense, DexGloveHOI, Apple Vision Pro, Quest); Ego-Exo4D egocentric challenge; exocentric kitchen and home captures (EPFL-Smart-Kitchen, ACE-Data-0, ParaHome); surgical egocentric RGB-D (POV-Surgery); bimanual monocular video (ARCTIC challenge).
clusters.attempted_fixes: New backbones (Mamba, ViT ensembles) give sub-millimetre gains. Probabilistic diffusion gives multiple hypotheses, but best-of-N selection needs ground truth and is slower. IMU gloves and EMG wristbands help but change hand appearance or fail across users. Large synthetic RGB-D data gives 2-3 percent. Fine-tuning on occluded frames still leaves error above non-occluded levels. Linear interpolation or discarding of low-confidence frames accumulates error over consecutive gaps. Multi-view input helps but needs calibrated rigs and does not generalize across layouts.

clusters.name: Two interacting hands lost, swapped or misplaced
clusters.statement: When two hands, of one person or of different people, come close, overlap or share an object, detectors and pose estimators lose a hand, swap left/right or owner identity, and misplace the hands relative to each other. As a result, bimanual estimation stays well below single-hand accuracy, and vision-based bimanual tracking and teleoperation break down.
clusters.description: Papers describe hand-over-hand occlusion, self-similarity of the two hands and close contact as conditions where current trackers fail outright, not merely degrade. Off-the-shelf pipelines (HaMeR) estimate the two hands independently, segment trackers swap left and right, identity errors at initialization propagate, and relative root placement errors stay at centimetres. Multi-person settings add bystander and co-worker hands and non-mirrored handover configurations with three or more hands. Fixes tried include per-hand detection pipelines, two-hand tokenizers, relighted and synthetic interacting-hand data with interhand attraction, multi-view dynamic matching, protagonist anchoring, and replacing vision with mocap suits for teleoperation.

evidence_items.item: VR hand tracking fails entirely on a bimanual handover because hand-over-hand occlusion breaks pose estimation; vision-based teleoperation also scores 0 percent.
SAM-Track confuses left and right hands and performs poorly when a hand is heavily occluded by objects or the other hand; HaMeR estimates the two hands independently, limiting bimanual performance.
Iterative refinement accumulates error when left/right hand identity is wrong at initialization.
Existing dual-hand 2D keypoint approaches can fail under severe occlusion or when the hands are far apart, requiring a custom per-hand detection pipeline.
VLMs cannot reliably tell the wearer's actions from the coworker's, especially when the two people's hands are close together.
A fixed clustering threshold fails when two hands are close together and move slowly; marker-free annotation methods handle at most two hands.
Two-hand analysis is hard due to self-similarity, articulation, small size and inter-hand occlusion, especially from a single image.
The method cannot reliably decide whether a two-hand interaction gesture occurs when the wrists come close.
Off-the-shelf hand reconstruction returns bystander hands, and camera-space heuristics cannot separate protagonist hands from bystander hands.
Single-view reconstruction leaves relative root errors of 28-52 mm between the two hands.
Single-person HOI findings, even bimanual, do not transfer to two-person handovers (non-mirrored hands, larger translations, three or more hands).
Interhand attraction fails when hand parts overlap seriously, because anchor pairs conflict and meshes are hard to separate.

benchmark_evidence: TeleOpBench ball_bimanual handover / success rate: vision 0 percent, VR 0 percent, vs Xsens mocap 100 percent, in simulation and real (1392)
InterHand2.6M / MPJPE: two hands 10.53 mm vs single hand 7.94 mm (1536)
HIC natural images / RRVE: IntagHand 67.11 mm, InterWild 23.59 mm vs about 20 mm on InterHand2.6M; Re:InterHand egocentric split 28.89 mm even after training on it (1185)
InterHand2.6M / MRRPE: relative root error 14.15 mm even with mixed real and synthetic training (1186)
ARCTIC / MRRPE right-to-left: 49-52 mm (1121)
ARCTIC HANDS 2024 bimanual category-agnostic / CDh: baseline 114.73, second place 100.33, winner 38.69, vs 11.3 for single-hand HOLD on HO3D (1528, 1529)
ADL4D annotation / unannotated frames: plain Dynamic Matching leaves 2005 of 6815 frames unannotated (1192)
clusters.settings: Monocular RGB bimanual manipulation (ARCTIC, InterHand2.6M, HIC, Re:InterHand); egocentric assembly with close two-hand contact (AssemblyHands); dual-arm teleoperation (TeleOpBench); multi-person handover and collaboration (HOH, CORE4D, IndEgo, ChildPlay-Hand, ADL4D); two-handed fingerspelling (BANZ-FS); surgical hands with instruments (OphNet-3D); egocentric touch detection with closely spaced bimanual events.
clusters.attempted_fixes: Per-hand detection pipelines and two-hand tokenizers that interpolate missing frames; errors compound under heavy occlusion. Relighted and synthetic interacting-hand data; it does not replace real data, relighting trained on single hands shows artifacts, and anchor attraction fails under serious overlap. Multi-view dynamic matching; it needs a hand in 3 views and still skips frames. Fitting one SMPL body at the egocentric camera to pick the protagonist. Replacing vision with mocap suits or exoskeletons for teleoperation.

clusters.name: Single hand, single object, no body context
clusters.statement: Most hand-object datasets and methods are restricted to a single hand, usually the right, interacting with one object without body or scene context. Bimanual cooperation, multi-person and multi-object interaction, and joint hand-body-object estimation therefore remain uncovered.
clusters.description: Many dataset and method papers list two-handed manipulation, bimanual pressure or bimanual grasp generation as future work, and one states that single-hand manipulation itself is still unsolved. Others describe fragmentation: full-body datasets lack hands, hand datasets lack body and global context, and modalities are split across datasets in short clips. Multi-person handover is described as qualitatively different from single-person bimanual interaction. Newer datasets extend coverage, but they stay in labs with heavy instrumentation and cover few people, objects or sites.

evidence_items.item: Two-handed manipulation is not covered; the authors consider single-hand manipulation still unsolved and leave hand cooperation for future study.
Single right-hand grasps only.
Trained on right-hand grasps only; left-handed and bimanual grasping are not modelled.
Only single-hand interactions are captured; bimanual pressure is left as an extension.
Single hand, single frame; extension to two-hand interaction is future work.
Single right hand with fixed MANO shape; hand-hand cooperation and bimanual manipulation are future work.
Existing 4D hand-object datasets are limited to one subject interacting with one object, restricting generalization.
Single-person HOI findings, even bimanual, do not transfer to two-person handovers.
Full-body datasets lack adequate hand tracking and hand datasets lack full-body and global context.
Most datasets cover single-object interactions or lack detailed hand motion; multi-object interaction with full-body and hand motion is a gap.
Modalities are fragmented across datasets and clips are short-horizon versus minutes-long household activities.
Existing 3D activity datasets annotate either hand or body pose; body truncation under limited viewpoints during bimanual tasks.
Full-body estimation is not integrated with action, forecasting or hand-object estimation.

benchmark_evidence: AssemblyHands-X / action recognition: hand plus body pose 78.7 percent vs body-only 57.5 percent; single-view hand-body PA-MPJPE 43.78 mm vs multi-view annotation (1170)
Assembly101 / pose-based recognition object accuracy 10.2 percent lower than video because hand poses carry little object information (1184)
Ego-Exo4D / ego body pose MPJPE 18.51 cm for the best test entry (1190)
Egocentric body pose survey / MPJPE: body-oriented camera 118.5 mm, outward-looking 121.1-152.1 mm (1091)
clusters.settings: Single-hand datasets and baselines (HOI4D, HOGraspNet, AffordPose, EgoPressure, HUG, DexCanvas; DexYCB and HO3D); multi-person handover and collaboration (HOH, CORE4D, ADL4D); body-hand activity datasets (EPFL-Smart-Kitchen, AssemblyHands-X, ATTACH, Ego-Exo4D, ACE-Data-0, HUMOTO, ParaHome, BOTH2Hands).
clusters.attempted_fixes: New bimanual and multi-person datasets (ARCTIC, OakInk2, GigaHands, ADL4D, HOH, CORE4D) and integrated ego-exo body-hand-object capture (ACE-Data-0, ParaHome, HUMOTO). All of them depend on lab mocap or dense rigs and still cover few people, objects or sites.

clusters.name: Hand-held object pose and masks lost during manipulation
clusters.statement: The 6DoF pose, and often even the mask, of the object being manipulated cannot be tracked reliably while hands occlude and move it. This holds especially from egocentric views, under fast motion and over long sequences. Trackers that work without interaction collapse once the hand grasps the object, pose recall stays near one third even multi-view with ground-truth masks, and active-object segmentation lags hand segmentation by about 60 points.
clusters.description: Dataset papers find that object perception, not hand perception, is the weakest link. Object pose trackers (BundleTrack, FoundationPose, FoundPose, DINOv2-based) succeed when only the camera moves but fail once the hand grasps and moves the object. The causes named are hand occlusion, rapid object motion, objects leaving the view, sensor noise, clutter, and contacted objects that do not move. Model-based trackers drift and need resets, manual masks or rigid-attachment gap filling, even in 70-camera rigs. Multi-view input and ground-truth masks help only modestly, and egocentric views are markedly worse than allocentric ones.

evidence_items.item: 6DoF pose of hand-held objects reaches only about one third recall at 5 cm, 5 deg even multi-view with ground-truth masks; ground truth for onboarding sequences is given only for the first frame because poses are hard to obtain when objects are hand-manipulated.
Category-level pose tracking drops from 86.5 on NOCS to 19.3 on HOI4D bottle; trackers work when only the camera moves but fail when the hand interacts (occlusion, rapid motion, sensor noise).
Object pose tracking loses track under fast motion or severe occlusion, accumulating errors (mask coverage 91.1 percent first frame vs 78.5 percent over the sequence).
FoundationPose frame-to-frame tracking fails during rapid movements; a mask-difference reset and SAM2 masks with human annotation were needed.
Active object segmentation stays weak: object mask AP about 24-28 on VISOR even fully supervised, far below hand AP of about 92.
Objects are harder than hands for long-term segmentation due to occlusion during manipulation and objects leaving view.
Object tracking can still fail under severe occlusion despite 70 cameras; gaps are filled by assuming the object moves rigidly with nearby joints.

All RGB object 6D methods perform worse under robot grasps than human grasps, and single-viewpoint stereo object tracking drifts during long-horizon manipulation unless multi-view silhouette consistency is enforced.
DINOv2-based object tracking misses objects under severe occlusion or strong sunlight.
Egocentric object reconstruction success rate drops to about 54 percent versus about 71-75 percent allocentric.
Objects cannot be recognized reliably in cluttered, occluded scenes, so ground-truth object labels are used.
Contacted-object segmentation fails for stationary objects because pseudolabels depend on object motion.
Object segmentation and tracking under multi-person occlusions during handover is listed as open.
Object-in-hand detection remains hard due to self-occlusion, hands occluding objects, and small, varied objects.

benchmark_evidence: HOT3D-Aria / FoundPose recall at 5 cm, 5 deg: 25.2 percent single-view, 33.8 percent multi-view, with ground-truth masks; Quest3 28.9 / 36.9 percent (103)
HOT3D-Quest3 / in-hand object segmentation mIoU: EgoHOS 33.1 percent, best 54.7 percent (103)
HOI4D / BundleTrack 5deg5cm: bottle 19.3 (86.5 on NOCS), toy car 9.7, mug 12.9 (1119)
EPIC-KITCHENS VISOR / object mask AP 24.03-27.77 vs hand about 92 (306); active object AP 25.7 vs hand 95.6 (1091)
HD-EPIC long-term VOS / object J&F: SAM2 27.0, Cutie 34.6 vs 89.1 for hands (1398)
HRDexDB / object ADD under robot grasp: FoundPose 8.74 cm, PicoPose 8.39 cm, GigaPose 13.80 cm, best refined 4.40 cm (1131)
ARCTIC egocentric / object success rate 53.9 percent for ArcticNet-SF (1121); best HANDS23 entry 74.07 percent (302)
GigaHands / object mask coverage 78.5 percent over the sequence vs 91.1 percent on the first frame (101)
Ego4D / state-change object detection AP 8-14 percent (1072)
OphNet-3D / instrument ADD-S: best RGB 70.79 percent, prior HOI methods 56.89-61.32 percent (1097)
clusters.settings: Egocentric headsets (HOT3D Aria and Quest 3, HOI4D head-mounted RGB-D, ARCTIC egocentric view); dense studios (GigaHands 51 views, ParaHome 70 views); dual Kinect plus FoundationPose (HUMOTO); kitchens (EPIC VISOR, HD-EPIC, Ego4D); multi-person handover (HOH); in-the-wild backpack rigs (SHOW3D); robot grasps (HRDexDB); surgical instruments (OphNet-3D); third-person in-the-wild video (ChildPlay-Hand).
clusters.attempted_fixes: Multi-view input (about +8 points recall), ground-truth masks, model-based trackers with mask-difference resets and manual SAM2 correction, rigid attachment to body joints to fill gaps, appearance-based rotation initialization for symmetric objects, multi-view silhouette consistency, markers on objects (which alter appearance) and dense camera rigs. None brings hand-held object tracking near the no-interaction level.

clusters.name: Small, thin, symmetric, transparent or reflective objects
clusters.statement: Hand-held objects that are small, thin, textureless, transparent, specular or metallic, or near-symmetric defeat both RGB feature matching and depth sensing. Their pose, shape, segmentation and annotation fail even when larger textured objects work.
clusters.description: Papers report near-total pose failure on small objects whose visible region is mostly covered by the hand, and depth ambiguity on thin elongated objects. ToF and RGB-D sensors give noisy or missing depth on shiny, dark or metallic surfaces. Transparent and reflective objects break radiance fields, segmentation, scanning and visual-feature fusion, and near-symmetric objects get the wrong rotation. Small moving objects are also segmented far worse than background in 4D point clouds. Capture teams resort to spray-painting, taping or marking objects, which changes their appearance.

evidence_items.item: Dice object pose fails because small visible regions under hand occlusion make the task ill-posed; thin or small objects score low.
Highly specular objects degrade pointmaps; thin elongated structures cause depth ambiguity; small objects amplify noise; uniformly textured objects lack features.
Featureless, highly reflective metallic instruments give noisy and incomplete RGB-D point clouds, making annotation unstable.
Shiny or dark objects give poor Kinect ToF depth and were spray-painted or taped.
All baselines fail on transparent, finely moving objects; foreground segmentation misses small, transparent, reflective or white objects.
Near rotationally symmetric objects with thin handles get wrong azimuthal rotation; small objects have lower annotation yield and accuracy.
COLMAP fails or performs poorly on small objects due to insufficient features; reconstruction of small, texture-less objects is open.
Microscope illumination overexposes instrument tips, degrading visibility and pose estimation.
Textureless or transparent objects mislead visual-feature fusion; grounding errors are worst at transparent, reflective and occluded regions.
Reflective, transparent or symmetric objects cause scanning feature-matching failures, mitigated with tapes and markers.
Accuracy drops on very small objects, and the point-cloud-only variant snaps to a nearby larger object when depth is unreliable on small targets.
4D point cloud segmentation does much worse on objects than background because objects are small, move flexibly and are heavily occluded.
Object pose annotation is not provided because small assembly parts make it hard.

benchmark_evidence: HOGraspNet / ADD-0.1D: dice 2.44, small_marker 28.29, credit_card 34.06, knife 38.17 (305)
SHOWMe / F-score at 5 mm: COLMAP+FDR 30.23 on small objects vs 47.93 on larger ones (1124)
HOI4D 4D point cloud segmentation / mIoU objects vs background: PSTNet 31.4 vs 72.6, P4Transformer 44.6 vs 77.7 (1119)
POV-Surgery / object control point error 41.56 px after fine-tuning (1128)
clusters.settings: Azure Kinect and RealSense RGB-D studios (HOGraspNet, HOH); monocular video reconstruction (SHOWMe, HOSt3R); surgical microscopes and synthetic surgical RGB-D (OphNet-3D, POV-Surgery); dense neural-field rigs (DiVa-360); egocentric in-the-wild capture (SHOW3D); egocentric RGB-D point clouds (HOI4D); tactile mocap scanning (TactiDex); egocentric grasping (HUG).
clusters.attempted_fixes: Spray paint, tape and markers on objects; switching from RealSense to Azure Kinect; appearance-based rotation initialization for symmetric objects; dropping glass-panel views; mocap-synchronized infrared imaging, proposed against overexposure. These alter appearance or only work in controlled capture.

clusters.name: Template-free reconstruction of unknown hand-held objects
clusters.statement: Without a pre-scanned or category CAD model, an unknown hand-held object cannot be reconstructed and tracked reliably from monocular video. Template-free pipelines depend on fragile SfM or keypoint registration and assume one hand, a fixed rigid grasp, a static camera and curated clear-view frames. They leave hand-occluded surfaces missing and fall far behind on bimanual sequences.
clusters.description: Most hand-object methods, datasets and trackers assume a known object template (scanned mesh, CAD or category model), which limits scalability to everyday objects. Template-free pipelines (HHOR, HOLD, HOSt3R, Gaussian-splatting entries in the HANDS challenges) depend on accurate camera or object registration. That registration breaks for textureless, small, thin and specular objects and under heavy hand occlusion, and the pipelines assume the grasp does not change. Hand-occluded regions remain unseen, so geometry is incomplete, and retrieval of external shapes fails for instance-specific or unseen objects. The single-hand HOLD baseline collapses on bimanual ARCTIC.

evidence_items.item: Most hand-object methods require a known object template; 3D foundation priors for template-free reconstruction are named future work.
Baselines assume known object models; articulated shape estimation of unknown objects is treated as an orthogonal problem.
Reconstruction quality depends on initial rigid transformations that are hard to get for texture-less objects or heavy hand occlusion; assumes a rigid grasp and static camera.
The method assumes the grasp is fixed while hand and object move together; specular, thin, small and uniformly textured objects degrade pointmaps and pose.
Category-agnostic HOLD handles only a single hand with near-constant contact and performs poorly in bimanual settings.
Hand-occluded object regions remain unseen and incomplete, motivating retrieval of external 3D priors that must exist in Objaverse.
Evaluation is restricted to objects with known category CAD models; reconstruction beyond known-category CAD models is not evaluated.
Pose estimation from handheld sequences is inaccurate and hand occlusions hamper learning the full object appearance.
Shape retrieval returns mismatched assets for instance-specific, articulated, deformable or unseen objects.
Model-free (CAD-free) object tracking from few-shot onboarding sequences is encouraged as an open direction.
Hands and objects cannot be tracked robustly under dexterous-grasp occlusion without dense multi-camera rigs and CAD models.
Accurate in-the-wild 3D hand and object pose cannot be produced without CAD models, multi-camera rigs or filtering that discards hard frames.
Pre-scanned or single-view-generated template meshes are needed for object 6DoF tracking.
The reconstruction task assumes a known object mesh.
Hand-object pose estimation is instance-level: object models are given during training and train and test use the same objects.

benchmark_evidence: SHOWMe / F-score at 5 mm: 73.5 with ground-truth transforms vs 37.6 with COLMAP and 20 with DOPE registration (1124)
SHOWMe / HOSt3R: F-score 56.4 percent with estimated vs 82.3 percent with ground-truth transforms; only 50.5 percent of frames within 15 cm and 15 deg (1112)
ARCTIC HANDS 2024 bimanual category-agnostic / CDh: winner 38.69, second place 100.33, vs HOLD single-hand HO3D level 11.3 (1528, 1529)
ARCTIC HANDS 2025 template-free / object F10mm 60.88 percent (GHOST) vs 81.78 percent (BIGS); CD_ICP 2.26 vs 1.36 cm^2 (1532)
EPIC-Grasps / SCA at IoU 0.8: 14.1 percent with category CAD known (1537)
GazeHOI / reconstruction success rate with known mesh: ArcticNet-SF 29.7, ArcticNet-LSTM 33.0, Keypoint Transformer 44.9 (1463)
clusters.settings: Monocular RGB video (SHOWMe, HO3D, ARCTIC HANDS 2024/2025 template-free tracks, EPIC-Grasps); static camera with the object rotated in hand (NVS-HO); egocentric multi-view (HOT3D model-free onboarding); in-the-wild backpack rigs (SHOW3D); dense studios and robot-grasp captures that still need scanned meshes (GigaHands, HRDexDB, GazeHOI, OakInk).
clusters.attempted_fixes: HOLD; keypoint-free pointmap reconstruction; SfM backends (COLMAP, HLoc, VGGSfM) or VGGT poses; Objaverse shape retrieval; 3D Gaussian splatting with 3D contact and merged-mask losses; camera refinement at about 1 GPU-day per sequence. All are offline, need curated frames, and assume rigid grasps or available assets. Diffusion and foundation shape priors are proposed but not shown.

clusters.name: Dynamic novel-view synthesis of hand-object scenes
clusters.statement: Dynamic radiance-field and Gaussian reconstructions of scenes with manipulating hands fail on the hands and the hand-held object. Interaction sequences score lower than object-only ones, moving-head egocentric capture breaks dynamic novel-view synthesis, and hand-held object NVS is limited by inaccurate object poses under hand occlusion.
clusters.description: Dense-camera dynamic-field benchmarks report blurry, noisy hands and lower PSNR on hand-object sequences, with training costs of about a minute per frame. Egocentric multi-view data shows existing 3D and 4D NVS methods failing with combined ego-motion, near-range hand motion, large disparities and occlusion; the gap is largest for close hands. For a static camera and a hand-rotated object, pose estimation is too inaccurate for NeRF or 3DGS to render the full object. The egocentric survey also names dynamic content and motion blur as open problems for egocentric 3D reconstruction.

evidence_items.item: All methods score lower on hand-object interaction sequences than object-only ones because of hand occlusion and complex hand motion; MixVoxels gives blurry, noisy hands.

Existing 3D and 4D NVS methods fail with combined ego-motion, near-range hand motion, large disparities and frequent occlusions; dynamic models are designed for object-centric or fixed-pose multiview video.
Pose estimation from handheld sequences is inaccurate, so NeRF/3DGS cannot fully render the object, and hand occlusions hamper learning full appearance; pose refinement gives only marginal gains.
Egocentric 3D reconstruction struggles under motion blur, unusual viewpoints and dynamic content.
12 of 51 views were removed for radiance-field reconstruction due to lighting issues.

benchmark_evidence: DiVa-360 / PSNR lower on interaction than object-only sequences by 2.73 dB (PF I-NGP), 1.98 dB (MixVoxels), 0.44 dB (K-Planes); 48-58 s training per frame (20)
Ego-1K / held-out PSNR: K-Planes 16.46, per-frame 3DGS 21.22, Spacetime Gaussians 24.76, stereo-guided 3DGS 29.12 (226)
NVS-HO / median foreground PSNR about 16 for the best baseline (Splatfacto with COLMAP poses) (1103)
clusters.settings: 53-camera table-scale dome (DiVa-360), 12-camera egocentric head rig (Ego-1K), static monocular camera with hand-rotated objects (NVS-HO), dense 51-view studio (GigaHands), egocentric wearable video (survey).
clusters.attempted_fixes: Per-frame I-NGP is temporally inconsistent, and stereo-guided 3DGS needs rectified stereo. Pose refinement during NVS training gives a marginal gain. Comparing COLMAP and VGGT poses shows COLMAP better but neither sufficient. Feed-forward pose-free NVS is proposed but does not yet scale to 100+ images.

clusters.name: Metric depth and absolute placement from RGB
clusters.statement: Monocular RGB estimators recover root-relative hand articulation but not metric depth, global translation, scale or the relative 3D placement of hand to hand and hand to object. Absolute errors are two to three times the Procrustes-aligned ones, errors lie mainly along the optical axis, and alignment-based metrics hide them.
clusters.description: Papers show large gaps between Procrustes-aligned and absolute errors, and several capture pipelines discard HaMeR depth entirely as unusable. Errors lie mainly along the viewing ray, so 2D projections align while 3D contact and relative distance are wrong, and weak-perspective MANO regression cannot localize the hand in world coordinates. The causes named are the scale ambiguity of a single view and inaccurate monocular depth priors; some benchmarks report only root-relative results for monocular methods. Stereo, multi-view triangulation and RGB-D help, while monocular metric-depth stages mis-scale.

evidence_items.item: Root-relative MPJPE 12.4 mm remains more than double the Procrustes-aligned 5.5 mm on DexYCB, showing global pose and scale error under object occlusion.
Monocular depth lifting errors lie mostly along the optical axis, caused by inaccurate depth predictions.
HaMeR's predicted depths were unusable due to severe inaccuracy, so only 2D keypoints with multi-view triangulation were used.
RGB-only pipelines remain ill-posed in depth, giving global translation and scale errors even when 2D projections align.
HOLD is accurate in 2D contact from the camera view but poor in 3D contact from other viewpoints and fails to estimate relative hand-object distance.
Procrustes alignment conceals errors in absolute position, orientation and metric scale.
HaMeR predictions look plausible from the top but reveal inaccuracies and scale ambiguity from side views.
SfM object point clouds and HaMeR hand translations are misaligned due to scale inconsistency and drift.
Weak-perspective MANO regression loses depth and cannot localize the hand in world coordinates.
HaMeR meshes lack accurate depth; RGB-only capture without depth makes pose estimation hard.
Lifting 2D affordance points to 3D with a single RGB-D camera produces z-axis errors.
True 3D data is not obtainable from a single 2D observation because of scale and depth ambiguity.
UmeTrack shows inaccurate relative depth of keypoints.
Single-view hand benchmarks report only root-relative error; no world-space result is reported for monocular methods.

benchmark_evidence: DexYCB / MPJPE vs PA-MPJPE: 12.4 mm vs 5.5 mm (4)
Ego-Exo4D hand challenge / MPJPE vs PA-MPJPE: winner 24.80 mm vs 8.31 mm (1526); POTTER 30.57 vs 11.14 mm (1190)
ARCTIC / relative root error: MRRPE right-to-left 49-52 mm (1121)
HOT3D-Aria / 3D lifting recall at 5 cm: StereoMatch 42.6 percent vs MonoDepth 11.1 percent (103)
HOT3D zero-shot / hand translation CT-p 0.196 m (1359)
OphNet-3D / MRRTE: 31.89 mm RGB vs 26.59 mm RGB-D (1097)
AnyHand test / unaligned MPJPE 14.29-14.98 mm and pre-alignment F@5 about 0.14 (1130)
InterHand2.6M / MRRPE 14.15 mm (1186)
OAKINK2 single-view HMR / RR-MPJPE 13.08-17.56 mm with no world-space result for monocular methods; multi-view world MPJPE 9.17 mm (67)
clusters.settings: Monocular RGB single image or video (DexYCB, HO3D, InterHand2.6M, ARCTIC, OAKINK2); egocentric headsets (Ego-Exo4D, HOT3D, AssemblyHands, UmeTrack challenge); multi-view piano capture (FurElise); surgical RGB vs RGB-D (OphNet-3D); single RGB-D affordance lifting (GLOVER++); egocentric pressure (EgoPressure); VLA pretraining from human video.
clusters.attempted_fixes: Stereo or multi-view triangulation instead of regressed depth; RGB-D input, which improves OphNet-3D by about 5 mm MRRTE; monocular metric-depth stages, which under-scale on HOT3D and over-scale on ARCTIC; extrinsic augmentation; contact losses that pull hand translation toward the object. All need calibration or depth that monocular settings lack.

clusters.name: Egocentric moving camera: drift and out-of-view hands
clusters.statement: From a head-worn or hand-held moving camera, current methods cannot separate camera ego-motion from hand and object motion over long sequences. World-space hand trajectories therefore drift by centimetres to decimetres. Hands at fisheye image edges, near the body or outside the narrow field of view are lost.
clusters.description: Several papers identify ego-motion error, not hand articulation, as the main error source for world-space hands. They note that manipulation itself breaks the static-world assumption that SLAM loop closure relies on. Head cameras miss interactions near the body, upper headset cameras often miss hands, hands and objects leave the frame, and fisheye distortion at image edges raises error. Methods that assume a fixed camera collapse under head motion, and the scale ambiguity of monocular reconstruction persists. Tried: device SLAM and VIO, metric-depth stages, body anchoring and offline optimization.

evidence_items.item: Egocentric hand methods have world trajectory error of about 98-102 mm, driven by ego-motion error; minutes-long takes drift.
Scale drift from monocular reconstruction persists; without loop closure or global optimization absolute trajectory error accumulates.
Joint world-frame recovery of ego-motion, contact and long-horizon hand-object state is unsolved; egocentric camera-frame estimates drift over extended manipulation.
Camera-space control signals entangle camera ego-motion with hand motion; the pipeline cannot tell whether a missing detection means the hand left the image.
Fisheye distortion at image edges degrades hand estimates and upper headset cameras often miss hands.
Manipulation breaks the static-world assumption, so no loop closure; wrist-camera VIO occluded by hand or object fails and drifts.
The method assumes a fixed camera; egocentric head motion would need explicit hand and camera motion decomposition.
Head-up cameras miss interactions close to the body; VQ3D camera poses are estimated for only 15 percent of queries.
Existing 3D and 4D NVS methods fail with combined ego-motion, near-range hand motion, large disparities and frequent occlusions.
SLAM drift, scale ambiguity and failure under fast motion or low texture remain open for handheld bimanual capture.
Hands are hard to track in the wild, especially in egocentric views where hands leave the frame.
Egocentric setups are infeasible for handover capture because of the limited field of view.
Rapid head motion, occlusion by hands or tools and narrow field of view make egocentric recognition ambiguous.

benchmark_evidence: ACE-Data-0 ego-view hands / world trajectory error: Dyn-HaMR and HaWoR about 98-102 mm vs best exocentric 63 mm (1363)
ARCTIC / world-space joint error: W-JPE 114.00, WA-JPE 46.91 for the best hand-controlled video method (1483)
HOT3D / arc-length ratio 0.466 without metric stage; hand translation CT-p 0.196 m (1359)
AssemblyHands / MPJPE: 20.31 mm rising to 24.85 mm as hands approach fisheye image edges (302)
ARCTIC / object reconstruction success: about 54 percent egocentric vs 71-75 percent allocentric (1121)
Ego-1K / PSNR: K-Planes 16.46, per-frame 3DGS 21.22 vs stereo-guided 29.12 (226)
H2O / action accuracy: HTT collapses to 2.89 percent on unseen egocentric camera 4 (1538)
clusters.settings: Project Aria, Quest 3 and Vision Pro headsets; Ego-Exo4D; HOT3D; ARCTIC egocentric view; daily-life and industrial egocentric video (HD-EPIC, Ego4D, IndEgo); head-mounted multiview rig (Ego-1K); handheld UMI-style grippers with head stereo-inertial SLAM (HiFi-UMI, YUBI); pseudo-labelling of public egocentric video (MINT).
clusters.attempted_fixes: Device SLAM and VIO (Aria MPS, ARKit, MegaSAM), a metric camera-trajectory stage trained on a small rig corpus, an SMPL body anchored at the camera to identify protagonist hands, offline SLAM with marker cubes, and stereo-guided reconstruction. Drift remains at centimetre level or worse, and the methods are offline.

clusters.name: No causal, temporally stable tracking under fast motion
clusters.statement: Per-frame hand and hand-object estimators produce jittery, temporally inconsistent output, and they drop frames or drift under fast motion and motion blur. The best benchmark results and annotation pipelines therefore depend on offline whole-sequence smoothing, interpolation or per-sequence optimization that cannot run causally in real time.
clusters.description: Challenge reports state that their networks have no temporal modelling and that regressed or triangulated joints jitter, so they apply offline Neural Smooth, Savitzky-Golay, Gaussian or Butterworth filters. Reconstruction and annotation pipelines rely on per-sequence optimization of tens of thousands of iterations or about a GPU-day per sequence. Diffusion models run at a few frames per second with temporal flicker. Pseudo-label pipelines and object trackers lose hands and objects during rapid motion and blur and interpolate gaps, accumulating error. Real-time uses (AR/VR, cobots, handover failure detection) are named as blocked because detection uses future frames. Proposed fixes are online temporal optimization, high-frame-rate capture, event cameras and extra lighting.

evidence_items.item: The temporal refinement (Neural Smooth) is an offline post-processing step, not real-time; per-frame predictions are jittery and inconsistent between 2D and 3D; turning it online is future work for AR/VR.
The network has no temporal modelling; triangulated joints are temporally unstable and need an external, non-causal Gaussian smoothing filter.
The best AssemblyHands method uses offline Savitzky-Golay smoothing over full sequences; fast fingertip motion drives high-error actions.
The annotation pipeline loses hands during rapid motion and blur; gaps are linearly interpolated or marked invisible.
Interpolating several consecutive missing frames gives inaccurate hand poses due to no direct observation and cumulative error.
Accuracy declines as signing speed rises; motion blur obscures finger-count differences.
Rolling-shutter RealSense imagers produce blurry frames under normal indoor light; a fixed clustering threshold fails when hand speed varies.
Regular CMOS cameras cannot handle hand-object action analysis in highly dynamic conditions.
Object tracking loses track under fast motion or severe occlusion during manipulation, accumulating errors.
FoundationPose frame-to-frame tracking fails during rapid movements; raw capture contains drift and joint jitter that artists must fix.
The pipeline is per-sequence offline optimization (45K iterations) on frames selected where hand and object were most clearly visible.
HHOR camera refinement costs about 1 GPU-day per sequence.
Offline detection uses future frames, which is not practical for a cobot that must detect live.
Baselines classify handover outcome only after the complete trial; online, early failure detection is open.
Diffusion pressure prediction flickers across adjacent frames and the base model runs at 2.8 FPS.
The 10-step diffusion sampler is slower than existing regressors (140 ms vs 40-50 ms).
HaMeR is per-frame, so Butterworth smoothing is applied.
HaMeR hand pose PCK drops on egocentric manipulation with fast hand motion and low-resolution imagery.

benchmark_evidence: UmeTrack challenge / MPJPE: 13.92 mm only after offline neural smoothing, 17.91 mm without (1530)
UmeTrack challenge / fingertip PCK AUC 70.81 percent vs overall 75.66 percent; smoothing plus optimization adds only 0.5 AUC (1531)
AssemblyHands / MPJPE: best 12.21 mm overall but 16.27 mm on fast inspect actions (302)
Hoi! kitchen / HaMeR PCK@0.15: 0.535 vs 0.844-0.893 on Ego4D, VISOR, New Days, attributed to fast hand motion and low-resolution egocentric imagery (225)
BANZ-FS / letter accuracy falls with speed; news interpreters sign at 4.59 vs about 1.30 characters per second (531)
EgoTactile / base model 2.8 FPS with temporal flicker (1387); cascaded diffusion hand pose 140 ms vs 40-50 ms for regressors (1543)
SHOWMe / HHOR camera refinement about 1 GPU-day per sequence (1124)
ATTACH / online detection marginally worse than offline; frame mAP 29.5 percent offline person split (1189)
clusters.settings: Egocentric headset tracking challenges (UmeTrack, HOT3D, AssemblyHands); monocular ARCTIC bimanual challenge video; object tracking in studios (GigaHands, HUMOTO, HMDO at up to 110 FPS); piano performance video (FurElise, PianoMotion10M); fingerspelling video; RealSense D435 multi-view rig (ADL4D); event cameras (EHoA); cobot assembly and robot handover failure detection (ATTACH, HFD); egocentric pressure diffusion (EgoTactile).
clusters.attempted_fixes: Offline smoothing filters and whole-sequence optimization, linear interpolation of missing frames, extra spotlights against blur, high-frame-rate capture and event cameras. One-step and consistency distillation for diffusion models and causal MS-TCN variants are proposed. The filters are non-causal and add little, and interpolation errors compound over long gaps.

clusters.name: Commodity RGB-D depth unreliable at hands and objects
clusters.statement: Commodity depth sensors (Azure Kinect ToF, RealSense, iToF) give noisy, quantized or missing depth exactly on hands, on small, thin, shiny, dark or reflective objects, at object boundaries and under motion. RGB-D hand-object methods therefore cannot rely on raw sensor depth, and large real datasets with well-aligned depth are scarce, even though depth measurably helps.
clusters.description: Capture papers report that shiny or dark objects had to be spray-painted or taped for Kinect ToF and that metallic tools give incomplete point clouds. Depth has missing values and ghost shadows at object boundaries and becomes inaccurate for far hands. Depth also measures skin rather than joints, and iToF is unreliable under motion. RealSense D435 point clouds were too imprecise for sim-to-real, and its rolling-shutter colour imager blurred. One paper found estimated depth better than real HO-3D sensor depth, and synthetic depth-noise models are heuristic. Where clean depth is available, RGB-D variants improve hand and object accuracy, and articulation and grasp methods depend on it.

evidence_items.item: Shiny or dark objects give poor Kinect ToF depth and were spray-painted or taped; Kinect depth is noisy at the rig's working distance.
Featureless, highly reflective metallic instruments give noisy and incomplete point clouds with RGB-D cameras, making annotation unstable.
Depth sensors give missing values and ghost shadows at object boundaries and become inaccurate when hands are far; single-view depth measures the skin surface, not the joint.
Real HO-3D depth maps are heavily quantized with missing values, and estimated depth gave better results than sensor depth; large datasets with well-aligned depth remain scarce.
iToF depth streams were not used because depth is unreliable under motion and phase ambiguity.
RealSense D435 point clouds were too imprecise for sim-to-real, so Azure Kinect was used instead.
Rolling-shutter colour imagers on D435 produce blurry frames under normal indoor light; spotlights were needed.
Articulation methods are too dependent on accurate depth; noisy scaled monocular depth breaks 3D lifting.
The point-cloud-only grasp model snaps to a nearby larger object when depth is unreliable on small targets.
The depth noise model for generated RGB-D data is a heuristic approximation; physically validated sensor-noise modelling is open.
Category-level tracking failures on HOI4D are attributed partly to sensor noise from the head-mounted RGB-D camera.
The articulated hand-object method relies on depth (partial point clouds) more than texture.
Lifting 2D affordance points to 3D with a single RGB-D camera gives z-axis errors.
RGB-D variants outperform RGB-only for bimanual hand and instrument pose.

benchmark_evidence: HO-3D v2 (RGB-D) / STA-MPJPE: prior Keypoint-Fusion 1.87 cm, AnyHandNet-D 1.09 cm (1130)
OphNet-3D / MPJPE 17.66 mm RGB vs 15.97 mm RGB-D; ADD-S 70.79 vs 76.31 percent (1097)
HOI4D / BundleTrack bottle 19.3 vs 86.5 on NOCS, attributed partly to sensor noise (1119)
Ego-1K / stereo cross-pair agreement within 1 mm: 0.0-3.1 percent for two stereo methods, 74.0 percent for FoundationStereo, evaluated without ground-truth depth (226)
clusters.settings: Multi-view and single RGB-D rigs with Azure Kinect or RealSense (HOH, ADL4D, HO-3D, HOI4D, DexGarmentLab, HUG, GLOVER++); egocentric iToF (Ego-1K); surgical RGB-D (POV-Surgery, OphNet-3D); RealSense L515 handover capture; Hoi! multi-view RGB-D articulated manipulation.
clusters.attempted_fixes: Spray-painting or taping objects, segmentation plus outlier removal, switching sensors, extra lighting, replacing sensor depth with estimated depth, heuristic noise models for synthetic RGB-D (not physically validated), and stereo foundation models.

clusters.name: Hand-object contact location and timing
clusters.statement: Where and when the hand touches the object cannot be estimated from vision to the needed precision. Reconstructed contact stays centimetres off, with interpenetration or floating, contact maps reach low IoU, frame-exact contact onset and release are rarely detected, and proximity is not distinguished from real contact. Instantaneous contact ground truth does not exist.
clusters.description: Bimanual and egocentric benchmarks report contact deviation of 3-4.5 cm, interaction-field errors of 1.5-3 cm even for challenge winners, and dynamic contact maps with mIoU near 0.2. Papers name self-occlusion of the hand-object gap, MANO misalignment with real hand geometry, small hand-pose errors that produce penetration, and the inability to tell proximity from real contact. Temporal contact events (onset, grasp, release) are ambiguous under ego-motion, occlusion and motion blur, and affordance learning from images gives only static 2D contact points. Measured contact (instrumented keyboards, wet paint, tactile gloves) exists only in special setups and often only as accumulated contact.

evidence_items.item: Egocentric ARCTIC contact deviation stays at 32.56 mm for the best entry; contact remains centimetres off.
Single-view reconstruction leaves a large hand-object contact deviation of about 39-45 mm.

Absolute contact accuracy remains low even for the best method; real-world datasets lack contact ground truth, the benchmark has only accumulated contact, and MANO annotations misalign with real hands.
Existing contact methods lack the temporal granularity to find contact onset; near-touch frames are ambiguous under ego-motion, occlusion and motion blur.
False negatives at grasp initiation and hallucinated lingering pressure at release arise from egocentric self-occlusion of the hand-object gap.
Spatial priors cannot tell whether proximity is real, force-transmitting contact; geometric metrics do not establish correct contact.
Slight hand pose errors cause hand-object interpenetration.
Kinematic fitting leaves floating or penetration artifacts during object interaction that require tactile-constrained post-optimization.
Vision-only reconstruction commonly shows incorrect or missing key presses; MIDI from the instrumented piano is needed.
Transitional stages grasp and release remain challenging even for the best network.
Accurate hand-object contact labels are very hard to obtain from images; HOI4D labels are not accurate enough for contact.
MANO and rigid object models cannot represent contact deformation, so a contactness heuristic imitates it.
Mutual occlusion makes the interaction area hard to observe, so contact-region deformation is hard to reconstruct.
Affordance learning from human video cannot yet supply time-resolved 3D contact, only static 2D contact points.
Stable contact is reconstructed for only a small share of in-the-wild grasp clips; scissors show near-total failure of stable contact.
Even the first-place stereo ensemble keeps a mean interaction-field error of 27.82 mm on unseen subjects.
Annotating the making and breaking of contact from RGB is difficult and noisy.

benchmark_evidence: ARCTIC egocentric / CDev: best HANDS23 entry 32.56 mm vs 27.97 mm allocentric (302); ArcticNet-SF 41.6 mm allocentric, 44.7 mm egocentric (1121)
DyTact-21 / accumulated contact mIoU 0.226, F1 0.378 for the best method (1535)
TouchMoment / AP at exact frame: 14.25 on HOI4D, 24.25 on TACO (192)
SHOW3D challenge / interaction-field mean ADE: first place 27.82 mm (1546); best internal model 15.74 mm with only 51.23 percent within 10 mm (1547); cross-domain 22.57 vs 13.82 mm (1099)
EPIC-Grasps / SCA at IoU 0.8: 14.1 percent; ARCTIC-Grasps scissors SCA-IOU 2.7 (1537)
FurElise / key-press F1 vs MIDI: 86.49 after refinement (578)
TactiDex / contact F1: kinematic baseline 0.557, best 0.738 (1395)
OakInk-Shape grasp generation / penetration 0.67 cm, sim displacement 1.21 cm; handover generation up to 1.57 cm penetration (1120)
ChildPlay-Hand manipulation stages / macro F1 51.2 percent (1539)
EPIC-VISOR / contact segmentation IoU below 0.45 for all methods (368)
clusters.settings: ARCTIC bimanual monocular and egocentric; SHOW3D egocentric stereo interaction fields; HOI4D, TACO and EPIC-Kitchens egocentric video; DyTact dense multi-view; HMDO deformable capture; piano with MIDI ground truth; tactile glove plus mocap (TactiDex, EgoTactile); third-person in-the-wild video (ChildPlay-Hand); affordance images (GLOVER++); static grasp synthesis (OakInk, AffordPose).
clusters.attempted_fixes: Interaction-field representations; 3D contact and merged-mask losses; tactile-constrained optimization; instrumented objects that supply contact (MIDI keyboard); wet-paint or thermal accumulated contact ground truth; contact-guided Gaussian surfels; and stereo surface reasoning, which is gated because correspondence fails under occlusion and blur. Errors stay at centimetre level and no per-frame ground truth exists.

clusters.name: Contact force and pressure invisible to vision
clusters.statement: Hand contact force and pressure during natural manipulation of arbitrary 3D objects cannot be measured without instrumenting the hand or object, and cannot be inferred from video outside the lab. Vision-to-pressure and vision-to-force models collapse on unseen views, interaction patterns, tasks and real scenes.
clusters.description: Force is called the causal signal of manipulation, yet it cannot be labelled manually and is absent from video datasets. Measurement relies on flat pressure pads, on tactile gloves, or on simulation-derived forces that are exact only up to the simulator. The gloves are uncomfortable, drift, cover the fingertips, miss small parts and change hand appearance. Vision-based pressure models trained in green-screen labs lose about half their contact IoU on unseen views or interaction patterns, and force estimators are off by several newtons outside lab conditions. Tactile signals are also heterogeneous across sensors and often reduced to binary.

evidence_items.item: Pressure sensing is confined to flat surfaces; arbitrary object surfaces would need hand instrumentation that hinders natural interaction.
Force is absent from egocentric datasets because it cannot be manually labelled; glove sensors are uncomfortable, unreliable over time and interfere with fine manipulation.
Vision-only HOI capture lacks force and contact information; sensing gloves provide them but change hand appearance and must be translated to bare hands.
Force estimation from observation alone is under-constrained; sensors alter contact mechanics; forces are derived from physics simulation, not measured.
Vision-to-tactile prediction on an unseen task reaches cIoU 0.457 vs 0.689 in-distribution.
Tactile force model errors are several newtons versus millinewton accuracy in the lab; visual force estimation degrades on force-demanding mechanisms.
Only binary tactile signals are studied; pressure, shear, sensor variation and tactile sim-to-real remain open.
Glove tactile sensors cannot register interactions with small parts.
Occlusion breaks pixel-to-pressure alignment in egocentric grasping; RGB models fail on rare interaction patterns without explicit hand and object pose.
Tactile-from-vision with PressureVision gives near-zero contact IoU in ego-view home capture.
Affordance learning from human video cannot supply force-sensitive affordances.
Capturing physically valid contact still requires mocap plus tactile gloves and post-hoc contact correction.

benchmark_evidence: EgoPressure unseen exocentric views / contact IoU 36.82 percent vs 62.11 percent on seen views (98)
HandSense dexterous HOI / PressureVision++ contact IoU 0.8 percent (190)
HT-Bench OOD task / vision-to-tactile cIoU 0.457 vs 0.689 in-distribution (1396)
EgoTactile unseen interaction patterns / C-IoU 31.8 vs 56.3; realistic scenes 49.6 (1387)
Hoi! / force RMSE: Sparsh 3.86 N; ForceSight 3.53 N vs 0.40 N on its own dataset (225)
ACE-Data-0 ego-view tactile / PressureVision near-zero C-IoU and V-IoU (1363)
EPIC-VISOR / contact segmentation IoU below 0.45 for all methods (368)
clusters.settings: Egocentric RGB with a flat pressure pad (EgoPressure); tactile gloves (EgoTactile, HT-Bench, FEEL, TactiDex, VTDexManip, Kaiwu, HRDexDB); handheld force-tactile gripper on articulated furniture (Hoi!); mocap plus simulated forces (DexCanvas); home ego-exo capture (ACE-Data-0); multi-person handover (HOH).
clusters.attempted_fixes: Pressure pads; piezoresistive and full-hand tactile gloves; glove-to-bare-hand video translation, which degrades in the wild; force-supervised pretraining; simulation-derived contact forces; diffusion pressure models with object metadata, which flicker and run at 2.8 FPS. Wrist EMG and explicit hand and object pose conditioning are proposed but not demonstrated.

clusters.name: Articulated and deformable objects under manipulation
clusters.statement: Objects whose shape changes during manipulation, both articulated parts and deformables, cannot be captured, tracked, reconstructed or simulated together with the hands at the fidelity available for rigid objects. Datasets treat objects as rigid or single-DoF, articulation estimators fail outside category priors when hands, clutter and noisy depth are present, and non-rigid contact deformation is not reconstructed.
clusters.description: Papers report that automatic tracking of articulated and non-rigid objects is unsolved and that articulation priors are category-specific and depth-dependent. Articulation estimators fail in the wild with clutter, hands and noisy monocular depth. Deformable hand-object reconstruction needs pre-scanned templates, uniform material and ten synchronized cameras, and covers only small deformations. Datasets typically have one articulation degree of freedom, treat compound objects as rigid or exclude articulated objects, and robot simulators lack stable deformable physics. Open-loop robot execution and HOI video generation also degrade when objects articulate or deform.

evidence_items.item: Fully automatic tracking of articulated and non-rigid objects is not solved; non-rigid objects get only segmentation masks.
Cannot generalize to novel categories because articulation priors are object-specific; relies more on depth than texture.
Current articulation methods are too dependent on accurate depth or fail in the presence of clutter and hands.
Monocular hand-object reconstruction fails on hand-deformable object interaction; the dataset holds only small deformations and the method needs uniform material.
All objects have only one articulation degree of freedom; articulated shape of unknown objects is open.
Compound and articulated objects are treated as rigid; no deformable objects.
PBD garment simulation is unstable and FEM does not capture garment deformation; grasps fail on occluded or heavily deformed regions.
Generation quality drops when objects undergo large transformations such as rotation or opening.
Ground truth covers only instrumented rigid objects, with no annotation of articulated, fluid or deformable state changes.
The simulator cannot handle deformables or fluids; only rigid and articulated objects are covered.
The dataset excludes articulated objects; extension to articulated objects is future work.
Open-loop execution without visual feedback fails on objects that shift or articulate.
Garment folding is hardest in transfer; deformable-object supervision is open.
Part-level pose tracking of articulated objects such as laptops fails under hand interaction.

benchmark_evidence: HOI4D articulated objects / 5deg5cm: best 35.99 percent, baselines 3.17-7.69 percent (1126)
HOI4D laptop parts / 5deg5cm: ICP 0.9 and 1.5, BundleTrack 24.2 and 12.2 (1119)
Hoi! / ArtiPoint type recall 26.9 percent, axis errors 47.06 and 63.76 deg vs 14.54 and 17.14 on Arti4D; ArtGS revolute distance error 0.321 m (225)
OphNet-3D / articulation MAE 11.17 percent RGB, 9.62 percent RGB-D (1097)
DexGarmentLab / sim-only real success 53.3 percent (Hang Trousers), 60.0 percent (Wear Hat) (470)
TASTE-Rob / grasp type classification error 67.8 percent before refinement (113)
clusters.settings: HOI4D egocentric RGB-D; ARCTIC one-DoF objects; Hoi! Aria glasses with articulated furniture; HMDO 10-camera deformable capture; GigaHands and TACO studios; surgical articulated instruments (OphNet-3D); simulators (Isaac Gym, Isaac Sim, ManiSkill3); UMI garment folding; egocentric grasping (HUG); HOI video generation (TASTE-Rob).
clusters.attempted_fixes: Category-level articulation priors with depth (ContactArt); deformation graphs over pre-scanned templates with dense views (HMDO); part-wise instrument scans; synthetic-only training (CAPTRA and ANCSH do not generalize); PBD and FEM simulation; garment structural correspondence. None generalizes to novel categories or monocular input.

clusters.name: Accurate 3D ground truth requires markers or dense studios
clusters.statement: Accurate 3D hand-object ground truth can still be captured only in two ways. Markers, sensor gloves, CAD scans and manual cleanup alter appearance and natural motion and fail under occlusion. Dense calibrated multi-camera studios lose accuracy steeply as views are removed. Realism and annotation accuracy therefore cannot be obtained together, and annotated data stays confined to labs and tabletops.
clusters.description: Dataset papers describe a trade-off between realism and annotation accuracy. Marker mocap loses, merges and mislabels markers under occlusion and requires annotator or artist cleanup. Markers and gloves contaminate RGB, can constrain hand poses, and let models learn the markers instead of the objects. Markerless annotation needs tens to hundreds of cameras, per-object scans and per-subject calibration, and error grows two- to three-fold with fewer views or egocentric-only capture. As a result, datasets are table-scale, single-room or single-site, and in-the-wild datasets lack dense 3D ground truth. Tried: marker inpainting, neural relighting, mobile backpack rigs, SAM2 with manual correction, learned annotators and dynamic matching.

evidence_items.item: MoCap marker data contain errors requiring manual cleaning; markers are lost under extreme occlusion, ghost markers appear and close markers merge or are mislabelled (same paper as 67).
Markers on objects widen the appearance gap to in-the-wild objects and a tracker could learn markers instead of the object; marker removal by inpainting cannot recover true appearance.
ArUco markers corrupt the RGB data and may influence natural motion; markerless capture is future work.
Considerable manual cleaning by artists was required; raw capture contains drift, tracking errors and joint jitter.
Lab mocap or dome setups lack diversity, while in-the-wild datasets lack dense accurate 3D hand and object ground truth.
There is a trade-off between environmental realism and 3D annotation accuracy; automated filtering discards hard frames.
Ground truth required a studio with 170 cameras and 469 lights; natural datasets captured with few cameras contain only simple poses.
Egocentric-only annotation error is 27.55 mm versus 4.20 mm with exocentric multi-view; high-quality labels need 8 static cameras plus a calibrated headset.
Training with fewer allocentric views raises hand MPJPE from 23.4 mm (8 views) to 49.0 mm (2 views).
Hand joint error grows as camera views are removed: 14.75 mm with 4 views versus 5.58 mm with 10.
Marker, depth and multi-view setups need controlled environments; triangulation works well only with many cameras (30+).
Markerless capture has no ground-truth hand pose; manual annotation under occlusion and motion is daunting.
Vision-based human-object tracking is too low-fidelity under multi-person occlusion to scale HOI data, so capture depends on indoor mocap.
Ground-truth poses for dynamic onboarding sequences are given only for the first frame, because poses are hard to obtain when objects are hand-manipulated.
Physically valid contact cannot be captured without mocap plus tactile gloves and post-hoc contact correction.
Mocap labels with 21 markers per hand still leave 3.6 percent invalid frames and 4.3 mm alignment error.
In-the-wild 3D hand datasets are lacking, leaving an indoor-outdoor domain gap.

benchmark_evidence: AssemblyHands annotation / MPJPE: egocentric-only 27.55 mm vs 4.20 mm multi-view; OpenPose triangulation fails on 40.2 percent of keypoints (1122)
HMDO / hand joint error: 14.75 mm with 4 views vs 5.58 mm with 10 views (1127)
ARCTIC / view ablation: hand MPJPE 23.4 mm with 8 views vs 49.0 mm with 2; object success 68.6 to 40.8 percent (1121)
Ego-Exo4D / PA-MPJPE 14.01 mm at 3 views vs 10.02 mm at 6 (1190)
BOTH57M / markerless mocap ground-truth error 31.4 mm overall, 6.51 mm hands vs manual labels (8)
EPFL-Smart-Kitchen / pseudo ground truth error about 3.30 cm hand, 6.22 cm body (461)
SHOW3D annotation vs manual labels / P90 MPJPE 16.48 mm during interaction (1099)
ADL4D / best markerless mode still skips 226 frames at 5.94 mm MPJPE (1192)
EgoEMG label reconstruction / 3.6 percent invalid frames, 4.3 mm marker-to-mesh error (1180)
clusters.settings: Optical marker labs (OakInk2, TACO, HOT3D, ARCTIC, DexCanvas, GazeHOI, TactiDex, EgoEMG); inertial suit capture (HUMOTO); dense RGB studios (GigaHands 51, ParaHome 70, Re:InterHand 170 cameras); multi-Kinect RGB-D rigs (HOH, ADL4D, HOGraspNet, OphNet-3D, DexH2R, EPFL-Smart-Kitchen); mobile backpack rigs (SHOW3D, EgoExo-Hands); instrumented kitchens.
clusters.attempted_fixes: Generative inpainting of markers; manual and artist cleanup; neural relighting of studio captures; mobile backpack rigs with headset mocap; SAM2 masks with manual correction; learned automatic annotators bootstrapped from manual labels; multi-view dynamic matching; keyframe labelling with propagation; contrastive pretraining on unlabeled in-the-wild video. Each trades away accuracy, scale or naturalness, or keeps a studio, marker or CAD dependence.

clusters.name: Scaled egocentric hand data rests on pseudo-labels
clusters.statement: Large egocentric and in-the-wild hand datasets rely on unverified pseudo-labels from monocular estimators or headset tracking (HaMeR, HaWoR, MediaPipe, ARKit, Aria MPS, VR SDKs). These labels are off by centimetres and drop or corrupt exactly the occluded and fast-moving frames, so the data that scales has no verified 3D hand or object ground truth.
clusters.description: Papers building scaled corpora for robot learning, action understanding or video generation state that their hand annotations are model predictions. These are imperfect under heavy occlusion and fast motion, with missing joints, outliers, jumps and spurious bystander tracks. Hard frames are filtered, interpolated or discarded, biasing the data toward easy views, and the machine annotators of earlier interacting-hand datasets are also named as possibly inaccurate. Downstream effects are measurable: action recognition and grasp oracles lose accuracy from tracking error, and some pose labels are judged too inaccurate to train pose estimators. Re-annotation with multi-view capture is listed as future work.

evidence_items.item: Hand annotations are model predictions and can be imperfect under heavy occlusion or fast motion; joint confidence is zero when fully occluded.
Hand joints are missing in some frames due to occlusion; for sources without dexterous labels, 3D joint quality depends on the landmark estimator and depth.
No ground-truth 3D labels; pretraining data contains errors from 3D reconstruction, and noise is accepted.
Hand pose labels are pseudo-labels from MediaPipe plus HaMeR, inferior under rapid motion and blur, requiring outlier filtering and interpolation.
Human data relies on consumer VR hand-tracking SDKs that can fail under heavy occlusion.
Hand tracking degrades under occlusion, making grasp labels too loose or too tight.
Annotations come from monocular reconstruction, filtered heavily, with undetected frames interpolated; low-confidence detections produce spurious tracks.
Assembly101 3D hand poses from an off-the-shelf egocentric tracker are often inaccurate under object occlusion.
Pseudo-labels from HaWoR and YOLO show outliers, jumps and missing intervals.
Pseudo ground-truth 3D pose has centimetre-level error against triangulated manual 2D annotations.
Assembly101 pose labels are not accurate enough for training pose estimators.
Real interacting-hand datasets are annotated by a machine annotator, which may be inaccurate.
Hand keypoints come from Aria MPS automatic estimates, so the hand benchmark is exploratory only.
SAM2 initial object masks needed manual correction in 74 percent of cases.

benchmark_evidence: Assembly101 / original egocentric-tracker annotations had about 85 percent higher error than the 4.20 mm multi-view result (1129)
AssemblyHands / verb accuracy: 54.7 percent from predicted poses vs 60.0 percent from annotated poses; UmeTrack poses 50.3 percent (1122)
HUG-Bench / grasp success: human-grasp oracle only 90-94 percent due to hand-tracking error; model 73.0 vs oracle 94.0 percent (1386)
EPFL-Smart-Kitchen / pseudo ground truth error about 6.22 cm body and 3.30 cm hand against triangulated manual labels (461)
HD-EPIC / SAM2 initial masks needed manual correction in 74 percent of cases (1398)
clusters.settings: Apple Vision Pro ARKit (EgoDex); Meta Aria MPS (Hoi!, IndEgo, HUG, HD-EPIC); VR headsets (Humanoid Policy); HoloLens and Kinect fusion (EPFL-Smart-Kitchen); aggregated egocentric corpora (OpenEgo); internet video labelled with HaMeR or HaWoR (PianoMotion10M, HandsOnWorld, VLA pretraining, MINT); Assembly101 tracker labels; machine-annotated InterHand2.6M.
clusters.attempted_fixes: Confidence filtering, outlier removal, linear interpolation, discarding uncertain clips, slowing human actions, metric rescaling stages, and multi-view re-annotation of a subset (AssemblyHands). Filtering removes exactly the hard frames, and the remaining labels stay unverified.

clusters.name: Estimators fail outside their training capture domain
clusters.statement: Hand and hand-object estimators trained on one lab dataset, subject pool, camera rig or headset layout lose a large share of their accuracy elsewhere, with errors growing from roughly 1.5x to several-fold. This happens on other datasets, in-the-wild scenes, new headset extrinsics, unseen views or interaction patterns, and specialised domains such as surgery and kitchens.
clusters.description: Cross-dataset tests between lab benchmarks (DexYCB, TACO, HOGraspNet, HO3D, OakInk splits, ADL4D) double or triple errors. Studio-trained trackers regress on in-the-wild captures because of object occlusion, backgrounds and lighting, and multi-view headset trackers overfit the training camera layout and collapse on another headset. Pressure estimators fail on unseen camera views and interaction patterns, and surgical and fingerspelling domains show the same effect. Papers attribute the gap to dataset bias imposed by the capture method, monotonous lab appearance, markers, and limited subjects and scenes. Joint multi-dataset training, extrinsic augmentation and in-the-wild pretraining narrow the gap only partly.

evidence_items.item: Hand pose estimators trained on one of TACO or DexYCB degrade strongly when tested on the other.
Studio-trained hand models (UmeTrack, HOT3D) regress on in-the-wild data, struggling with object occlusion and novel backgrounds or lighting.
Without extrinsic perturbation augmentation the model collapses on HOT3D because of camera-layout mismatch with training data.
The hand tracker overfits to the camera configuration seen at training, so two-view mode degrades across headsets.
Models trained on existing datasets generalize poorly to other datasets; dataset bias follows the conditions imposed by the annotation method.
Off-the-shelf state-of-the-art hand pose methods fail on egocentric surgical data before fine-tuning.
Learned annotators and hand mesh recovery generalize poorly across datasets; cross-dataset errors exceed 33 mm.
Pressure estimation degrades strongly on exocentric camera views unseen during training.
HMR error rises when test subjects or objects are unseen.
The annotator model degrades on a new camera configuration and novel objects before refinement.
Action recognition collapses on an unseen egocentric camera.
2D pose models trained on CORE4D-Real or BEHAVE lose accuracy when transferred to the other dataset.
Lab-trained fingerspelling models drop sharply on broadcast and web video.
Contrastive pretraining on in-the-wild hand images gains only about 4-5 percent on egocentric AssemblyHands versus about 15 percent on FreiHand.

benchmark_evidence: DexYCB to TACO / MPJPE: 39.54 mm; TACO to DexYCB 76.20 mm (88)
HOGraspNet to DexYCB / MPJPE 42.65 mm (PA 9.36 mm); HO3D-trained 57.31 mm (305)
Cross-dataset HMR / root-relative MPJPE: 33.34-54.76 mm vs about 12-14 mm within dataset (1192)
SHOW3D / MKPE: 22.2 mm (UmeTrack-trained) and 19.6 mm (HOT3D-trained) vs 14.3 mm with all three training sets (1099)
EgoExo-Hands / MKPE: 16.28 mm vs 9.48-10.95 mm in-domain; 22.59-24.78 mm single-source (1534)
HOT3D challenge / MPJPE 184.27 mm without extrinsic augmentation, 21.66 mm with it, vs 13.92 mm on UmeTrack (1530)
HOT3D-Quest3 / MKPE: UmeTrack-trained 24.2 mm vs 10.9 mm after joint training (103)
OakInk-Image / MPJPE 12.10 mm (view split) to 18.04 mm (subject split) (1120)
Hoi! kitchen / HaMeR PCK@0.15 0.535 vs 0.844-0.893 on Ego4D, VISOR and New Days (225)
EgoPressure unseen exocentric views / contact IoU 36.82 vs 62.11 percent on seen views (98)
POV-Surgery / MPJPE without fine-tuning 77.46-115.67 mm (1128)
BANZ-FS / letter accuracy: Lab-trained models about 92 percent on Lab vs about 30-37 percent on News and Web (531)
H2O / action accuracy collapses to 2.89 percent on unseen egocentric camera 4 (1538)
clusters.settings: Lab-to-lab (DexYCB, TACO, HO3D, HOGraspNet, ADL4D, CORE4D-Real vs BEHAVE); lab-to-wild (SHOW3D, EgoExo-Hands, HIC, Hoi!); cross-headset (UmeTrack to HOT3D, Aria to Quest 3); unseen views and interaction patterns (EgoPressure, EgoTactile); clinical domain (POV-Surgery, OphNet-3D); unseen subjects and objects (OakInk, EgoEMG); fingerspelling across lab, broadcast and web video.
clusters.attempted_fixes: Joint multi-dataset training, extrinsic perturbation augmentation, contrastive pretraining on in-the-wild hand images, relighting and diffusion pose transfer (partial or shown only qualitatively), and glove-to-hand translation. None removes the gap.

clusters.name: Synthetic hand data cannot replace real data
clusters.statement: Synthetic hand and hand-object images cannot yet replace real captured data for training: synthetic-only training trails real training by large margins, and gains saturate as more synthetic data is added. The gap is attributed to photorealism, the realism of grasps and approach motion, lighting consistency, sensor noise, and missing arm and scene context.
clusters.description: Benchmarks of synthetic data for egocentric detection, interacting-hand pose, RGB-D hand pose, articulated object pose and handover prediction all report that synthetic-only training is markedly worse than real-only. They also find that synthetic data helps mainly when real labels are scarce and that gains plateau at a few million samples. Named causes include photorealism, inaccurate grasps, no model of the hand approaching the object, composited lighting, missing forearm context, and clean depth without sensor artifacts. Domain adaptation and mixing reduce but do not close the gap.

evidence_items.item: A synthetic-to-real gap of about 30-40 percent AP persists; synthetic data cannot replace real data, attributed to photorealism, grasp accuracy and limited diversity.
Training on 100 percent synthetic data degrades performance below the real-data recipe; in-domain gains saturate beyond 2-4M added samples.
Training on synthetic RenderIH alone performs worse than training on real InterHand2.6M; the synthetic data is meant to reduce, not replace, real data.
Composited images degrade performance on natural HIC images due to foreground and background lighting inconsistency.
Synthetic data does not model the motion of the hand approaching the object.
Synthetic-only trained CAPTRA and ANCSH cannot generalize to rich hand-object interaction scenes.
Synthetic HOI data lacks photorealism.
Glove-to-hand synthesis quality degrades in unseen in-the-wild settings.
Handover datasets are mostly synthetic without real sensor noise, causing a sim-to-real gap.
The diffusion pose-transfer data is shown to help only qualitatively; quantitatively validated in-the-wild synthetic data is still missing.

benchmark_evidence: EPIC-KITCHENS VISOR / overall mask AP: synthetic-only 9.88 vs real-only 45.33; out-domain synthetic on ENIGMA-51 0.21 (306)
InterHand2.6M / PA-MPJPE: RenderIH-only 13.50 mm vs real-only 6.76 mm; mixed 5.79 mm (1186)
Tzionas real / error triplet: RenderIH-only 22.11/25.8/47.7 vs 11.38/11.1/19.9 for real training (1186)
HO-3D v2 / PA-MPJPE 7.5-7.7 mm reduced only about 2-3 percent by AnyHand synthetic data (1130)
HandSense in-the-wild / mean opinion score gap to real 1.53-1.65 (190)
clusters.settings: Egocentric HOI detection (VISOR, EgoHOS, ENIGMA-51); interacting-hand pose (InterHand2.6M, Tzionas, HIC); RGB and RGB-D single-hand pose (HO-3D, FreiHAND); synthetic surgical data (POV-Surgery); articulated object pose (HOI4D); RGB-D handover video generation.
clusters.attempted_fixes: Unsupervised domain adaptation, mixing real and synthetic data, neural relighting, biomechanical pose filters and physics-simulated grasps, diffusion pose transfer (shown only qualitatively), and heuristic depth-noise models. None reaches real-data performance with synthetic data alone.

clusters.name: Forecasting and generating hand-object motion
clusters.statement: Forecasted and generated hand-object motion loses accuracy within one to three seconds and degrades on unseen object geometry and long multi-step tasks. It is often physically invalid, with interpenetration, floating hands, wrong contact and unstable grasps, and long-horizon text-driven bimanual manipulation cannot be planned end to end.
clusters.description: Benchmarks show forecasting errors of several centimetres and tens of degrees that grow with horizon and with novel tools, objects and subjects. Generative forecasters are worse than predictive ones, and anticipation is near floor under head motion. Synthesis methods produce penetration and unnatural contact unless guided. Generated videos show unnatural grip changes and hide invalid physics, and synthesized hand renders float or penetrate. Long-horizon LLM planning fails completely beyond five primitives. Tried: text and gaze conditioning, guidance, physics post-processing, refinement stages, LLM planning with search, and model scaling, which saturates.

evidence_items.item: Forecasting errors rise for the right hand and tool under novel geometries; generative forecasters have far larger errors; grasp synthesis has more collisions on unseen tool geometries.
Forecasting baselines degrade on unseen object shapes; interaction synthesis produces inter-penetration and unnatural contact.
Trajectory prediction error grows with horizon, from 0.031 m at 1 s to 0.053 m at 3 s.
Guidance-free methods suffer contact inconsistencies and penetration errors; naive guidance adds motion distortion.
LLM primitive planning succeeds only 36 percent overall and fails for tasks with more than five primitives; no end-to-end text-to-manipulation framework exists.
The fine-tuned video model produces unnatural grip changes during manipulation.
Diffusion-generated motions float above keys or press wrong keys.
Model scaling saturates; an ultra-large variant performs worse on all metrics.
Generated video hides invalid physics: contact drift, implausible motion and depth-ordering errors.
Hand movement forecasting suffers from drastic head movements and stochastic futures.
Naive hand render overlay causes penetration, floating and wrist artifacts; temporal and multi-view consistency of generative hand video is open.
Diverse, physically validated RGB-D handover data cannot yet be generated, and handover intention for unseen irregular objects is not anticipated reliably.
Hand-object motion forecasting remains challenging due to rapid, complex motion patterns.

benchmark_evidence: TACO / forecasting: generative baselines 54.9-70.5 mm right-hand MPJPE and 52.8-88.2 deg tool rotation error; best predictive 28.8-36.6 mm (88)
GigaHands / MDM forecasting: 69.3/62.3 mm hand MPJPE, 47.6 mm object translation, 67.5 deg rotation; text-to-motion R-Precision top-1 27.2 vs 77.4 upper bound (101)
CORE4D unseen objects / human joint error 186.4 mm vs 170.8 mm seen (121)
OpenEgo / 3D hand trajectory AED 0.0491 at 0.5 s to 0.1045 at 4.0 s (1374)
SHOW3D / 6DoF forecasting translation error 30.4 mm at 30 frames with text, 42.7 mm without (1099)
OakInk2 / planning success 36 percent overall, 0 percent beyond five primitives; generated motion perceptual score 3.64 vs 4.66 for data (1456)
TACO unseen geometry / grasp synthesis collision ratio ContactGen 10.40 to 17.56, HALO-VAE 2.39 to 11.11 (88)
GazeHOI unseen objects / MPVPE 118.7 mm, FOL 150.2 mm (1463)
Ego4D / short-term object interaction anticipation Top-5 mAP about 2 percent (1072)
